frozen_by: operational resume of the zero-delta producer run 39091660737, from persisted snapshot b293c45a
why_this_measurement_exists: Cycle 39086856920 froze and ran the five-falsifier served-artifact benchmark against ONE accepted served packet (rebuilt-39027045675) and three of the five falsifiers FIRED. A single-packet firing does not tell the product what to do: if the defect is a property of the SERVE PIPELINE it must be repaired upstream of every served packet, and if it is a property of that one packet it is not an ingestion defect at all. The accepted direction states explicitly that the DO-NOT-SERVE order on served packet 38839347028 'is NOT superseded by the rebuilt-packet verdict; both stand', so 38839347028 is a SECOND accepted served packet of record, not the same bytes. Measuring the SAME frozen falsifier family against it is therefore a discriminating cross-packet experiment on different bytes, not a forbidden byte-identical re-measurement.
question: On the SECOND accepted served query-map packet (38839347028), do the falsifiers that fired on the rebuilt-39027045675 packet fire again? I.e. is the falsification a property of the serve pipeline (systemic, upstream ingestion defect) or of that one packet (artifact-specific)?
product_decision_unlocked: Whether Product must add an upstream id-hygiene / adversarial-seed / date-scope ingestion repair that applies to every served packet, or whether the three fired falsifiers are confined to the rebuilt packet and must instead be handled inside the rebuilt-packet serve gate. The direction's Product lane carries an ordered repair list (RF1..RF5) that does not currently include a served-bundle ingestion repair; this measurement is what would put one there or rule it out.

transfer_anchor.instrument_note: the instrument is used BYTE-IDENTICALLY; the falsifier ids and rules below are re-stated verbatim from the accepted hypothesis and no instrument code is changed by this cycle, so the 39086856920 record stays reproducible.

success_rule: FROZEN BEFORE ANY ROW WAS READ. Verdict is BENCHMARK_VALID_WITH_FALSIFICATION when at least one falsifier fires; BENCHMARK_VALID_NO_FALSIFICATION only when every falsifier below is refuted. A falsifier that cannot be evaluated from the artifact is reported not_measurable with a reason and is NEVER counted as a pass. NOT_APPLICABLE is not a pass. THIS RUN'S SUCCESS RULE IS THE TRANSFER QUESTION, WHICH IS NOT IN THE INSTRUMENT: the instrument emits a per-packet verdict, and the transfer verdict (SYSTEMIC / PACKET_SPECIFIC / INCONCLUSIVE) is derived by comparing the two accepted per-packet records and is published beside both, never in place of them.

falsifiers.rule: count(decisions whose canonical_url is absent, or scheme != https, or host != mcp.opencaselaw.ch) == 0
falsifiers.why: the product claim under test is a SOURCE-LINKED bundle; a jurist click must land on the real OpenCaseLaw decision record

falsifiers.rule: count(decisions whose decision_id is empty/whitespace, or matches a known upstream placeholder/HTML-fragment shape) == 0
falsifiers.why: a decision id is the map point key, the citation anchor and the dedupe key; an unusable id is silently unusable as all three
falsifiers.reused_from: evaluation/retrieval_gate/id_hygiene.py documents the two upstream placeholder shapes (ge_gerichte_[pjdoc NNNN] template placeholders and raw ch_vb__td_class__... HTML fragments); the shapes are re-listed in the instrument and not re-derived

falsifiers.rule: count(decisions missing any of x, y, cluster_id) == 0
falsifiers.why: the clickable map is the product; a decision with no coordinates and no cluster cannot be placed or inspected

falsifiers.rule: count(decisions with a parseable decision_date before 2000-01-01) == 0
falsifiers.why: the master prompt scopes the base map to 'from 2000 onward'. This is a DISCLOSED scope measurement, not a frozen bar: the mission text states the window but no accepted gate family measures it, and a pre-2000 hit is not automatically wrong (Swiss case law has no 2000 cut-off in law). The falsification is of the PRODUCT's retrieval relevance claim, not of the corpus.
falsifiers.interpretation_rule: a non-zero count FALSIFIES the claim that the served top-rank set is scoped to the mission window. It does NOT by itself falsify source validity, and it MUST NOT be reported as a frozen-bar failure.

falsifiers.rule: count(decisions whose provenance field carries an 'adversarial' marker) == 0 in a PRODUCTION served packet
falsifiers.why: ocl:adversarial.* rows exist so the benchmark battery has hostile cases. If they survive into the packet the product serves, then every recall/geometry number computed over that packet is computed partly over synthetic rows. This is the single most product-relevant falsifier in this instrument.
falsifiers.interpretation_rule: a non-zero count means the served artifact is not a clean production observation. It does NOT mean the product's retrieval is bad; it means the artifact cannot be read as a production observation.

transfer_rule.SYSTEMIC: a falsifier FIRES on BOTH accepted served packets -> the defect is a property of the serve pipeline and needs an upstream repair that applies to every served packet
transfer_rule.PACKET_SPECIFIC: a falsifier FIRES on exactly one accepted served packet -> the defect belongs to that packet's own serve gate and is NOT an ingestion defect
transfer_rule.INCONCLUSIVE: a falsifier is NOT_MEASURED on either packet -> no transfer claim is made and the falsifier is reported as not measured, never as passed
transfer_rule.note: two packets is a small population. A SYSTEMIC label is the operative one because it demands an upstream fix; a PACKET_SPECIFIC label is provisional on the second packet. The population size is disclosed beside every transfer verdict and is NOT upgraded by repetition.

claim_ceiling: This instrument can only say whether a served packet's source identity, id usability, map completeness, date scope and adversarial-seed cleanliness hold, and whether those findings TRANSFER across the two accepted served packets. It cannot say the map helps a jurist, cannot move any accepted bar, and cannot say that two packets establish a pipeline-wide property.
